items.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024
items.q: Paul Simon I think is in-between. I don’t think he — he does hire arrangers but then at other times he’ll just work with his band and talk about what he wants.

ctx.x: So these fellas like this, they have arrangers who write out the horn parts for the most part. Is that correct?

Yeah. For the most part, yeah. I mean the Stones for instance did not, and we would use whatever, at that time Bobby Keys, who was kind of their most important and main sax guy, he recorded all those original solos on “Brown Sugar” and “Rip This Joint” and all the tenor solos were played by Bobby. And Bobby was, you know the section leader for sure and so we would kind of — would interface with Bobby in how we were going to — what horn lines we were playing. So occasionally they would ask us to come up with some…
about what he wants. People will kind of add their input in kind of an organic creative process.
